steps.what: Monitor virus protection on email applications
Draft a software change for virus protection

loop.input: alert rows and the rule template
loop.output: a change that cites rule ids only
loop.check: Every cited rule id is on the queue
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any sentence with no rule id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a held message is legitimate is not a fixed lookup

steps.what: Maintain the queue virus protection held

tasks.design: Virus and mail alerts land on a {BI} view. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts a protection change from alert ids only. The systems administrator signs that version. The {OPS_SYSTEM} applies it. Mail the rule cannot class stays in a queue. Message bodies are not stored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protection changes were typed on the console from memory, so a later review could not see which alert the change used.
tasks.enabler_now: Mail and virus tools can export an alert id, a rule id and a count without the message body.
tasks.still_hard: A quarantine that might be a real message still needs a person, and a bad rule can block the firm.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs the virus protection change and releases mail a rule should not keep.

ambition.what: Review virus protection exceptions every week instead of when the queue overflows

tasks.altitude: Less time collecting alert screenshots. The administrator can refuse a protection change that cites no alert.

reach.task: Ask for release of a held message
reach.learn: Which protection rules are signed and which mail is still waiting

evidence.claim: Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service for mid-size firms that speeds investigation, while a person still decides what to change.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. This design records rule id and result, not message bodies.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to live mail protection is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is configuring, monitoring and maintaining email applications and virus protection software.
Input contract: alert id, rule id, application id, count, owner. Producer is the protection export. Rows with no rule id stay on the manual queue.

Native filters are configured before custom code. The design does not read staff mail. Consent would be a different design. The modest meeting prior overstates the task: time is on the console and the quarantine.
unknowns: Who may release a held message when the administrator is away.
Whether a supplier hosts the mail application.
Which rules have no job interface.
research_questions: What share of quarantined mail is later released?
How many protection rules have no owner?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits the protection draft before signing
Quarantine review stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Adjust filters when a new mail application is added

approvals.approved_version: email protection version signed in this review
the same signed email protection version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes alerts stay unstructured, so the draft rarely fires and changes stay manual. The high case assumes signed rules apply, while every quarantine exception still takes administrator time. No unattended rule change is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with users about system problems

steps.what: Draft solutions for existing system problems

loop.output: up to two solutions that cite a solution id
loop.check: Each solution cites a solution id on the known list
loop.stop: If none matches, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A new problem phrasing does not match a solution by a fixed table

steps.what: Confer with network users about solutions
Record the solutions users will try

tasks.design: The system user describes the problem on a {HELPDESK} form. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts known solutions for the administrator to check. The conferral itself stays a conversation. Only the solution they agree is written back to the ticket.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problems arrived as unstructured mail, so similar solutions were retyped and the user still had to repeat the story.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can hold a system id and a short problem statement that a known-solution note can key on.
tasks.still_hard: The user has to recognise their own problem, and a wrong solution said aloud is hard to take back.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator confers with the user and decides which solution fits this problem.
tasks.altitude: Preparation is shorter. The conversation stays with the administrator, who can ignore a draft that does not fit.

reach.task: Try the solution agreed in the conversation
reach.learn: Which solutions were offered and which problem is still open

evidence.claim: Conferring about a system problem is a conversation. A prepared note can shorten the start. It does not replace the talk.
Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category and draft a knowledge item for a person to review.
Digest [S15] is a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, with no published baseline, so this design does not count a drop in tickets as time saved.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task ends when the user and the administrator have conferred and the agreed solution is on the ticket. Doing the fix is a later task.

Input contract: ticket id, system id, problem statement, user name. Producer is the system user. If the form is empty the administrator types the same fields from the conversation and marks them manual.
The conversation stays person to person. Native ticket forms are configured before custom code. A draft solution is not sent to the user unread.
unknowns: Which problems have no matching known solution.
Whether users will use the form or keep writing mail.
Who covers the conversation when the administrator is away.
research_questions: What share of problems already has a known solution?
How often does the user reject the first solution?

already_counted.description: Administrator checks a weak solutions draft before the talk
The conferral with users stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Add a known solution after the same problem appears again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most problems are new, so the note is empty and the conversation is unchanged. The high case assumes a useful note, while the conferral itself is not treated as saved. No ticket-volume claim is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor consoles and grant network access

steps.what: Operate master consoles to monitor performance
Read computer systems and networks performance
Sign computer network access for this user
Coordinate network use when consoles clash

tasks.design: Master consoles feed a {BI} view of computer systems and networks. Access requests arrive on a {WORKFLOW} form with a user, a system id and an end date. The systems administrator signs that request. Only that version is granted. A clash on the consoles stays a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access was granted from chat with no end date, and performance notes were not tied to a system id.
tasks.enabler_now: Consoles can export a system id and a threshold breach, and the request form can carry an end date.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a breach matters, and that a person should have access, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs network access and decides when consoles show a clash that must be coordinated.

ambition.what: Small-site staff can request network access without waiting for a visit

tasks.altitude: Less time copying performance figures. The administrator still operates the consoles and can refuse an access request.

reach.task: Read which network access is signed before a design change
reach.learn: Which access grants are current and which performance breaches are still open

evidence.claim: Operating master consoles is still a person watching the systems. The part that repeats is copying figures and retyping access.
Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service that speeds investigation for mid-size firms, while a person still decides.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. An access log should record the grant, the system and the end date, not how the person works.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended grant of network access is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is operating consoles to monitor performance and to coordinate network access and use.

Input contract: system id, threshold, user id, access end date, request id. Producer of the breach is the console. Producer of the request is the system user. A request with no end date is not granted.
Native console views are configured before custom code. The meeting-heavy prior overstates this task: the time is at the console. Access logs are not used to watch staff.
unknowns: Who may grant access when the administrator is absent.
Whether some access is approved by a manager rather than the administrator.
research_questions: What share of access grants has no end date today?
How often does a threshold breach need a person the same hour?

already_counted.description: Time operating consoles stays with the administrator
Access signature stays with the administrator
Clash coordination stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Revise access fields when a new system type is added
Users resubmit requests that lack an end date

approvals.approved_version: network access version signed for this request id
the same signed network access version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes consoles have no export, so monitoring stays fully manual and only the request form is new. The high case assumes grants apply after a signature, while operating the consoles and coordinating a clash stay manual. No unattended grant is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep network function logs and repair records

steps.what: Sign which network functions to keep

loop.input: repair notes and the record form
loop.output: records that copy only stated fields
loop.check: Each filed record has a system id and a repair id that appear in the note
loop.stop: If a system id is missing, leave the record blank and stop that note
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text repair prose does not map to fields by a fixed table

steps.what: Maintain records related to a repair gap

tasks.design: The systems administrator signs which network functions may be extracted. The {OPS_SYSTEM} writes that extract. Maintenance and repair records arrive on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded pass files complete records and leaves gaps for a person. The extract stores job facts, not staff activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs were copied by hand into documents, and repair notes had no system id, so a later reader could not tell what was missing.
tasks.enabler_now: Devices already emit function logs. A signed list of functions and a record form with a system id are enough to file them.
tasks.still_hard: A repair note with no system id cannot be filed safely, and a log that watches people is out of bounds.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator signs which functions are logged and finishes records the form cannot complete.

ambition.what: Check log gaps every week instead of only when an audit asks

tasks.altitude: Copying logs leaves the week. Gaps and the choice of what to log stay with the administrator.

reach.task: Read maintenance records before a design change
reach.learn: Which functions are in the current extract and which repair records are incomplete

evidence.claim: Network devices already write function logs. The human work is choosing what to keep and filing repair notes that arrive as prose.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. A function log should record the event and the system, not staff activity.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is logs of network functions plus maintenance and repair records. Watching how staff work is not this task.

Input contract: function id, system id, event time, repair id, result. Producer of the extract list is the administrator. Producer of a repair record is the person who did the repair. A record with no system id is not filed.

Native log exports are configured before custom code. The low meeting prior fits a records task. Logs are not later reused to score staff. If that were proposed, it would need a separate consent step this design does not take.
unknowns: Which devices keep logs the firm cannot export.
How long function logs must be kept.
Who writes the repair record when a supplier did the work.
research_questions: What share of repair records arrives with no system id?
Which network functions are logged today with no named purpose?

already_counted.description: The choice of which functions to log stays
Review of filed repair records stays
Gap closing on repair records stays

incremental.description: Update the function list when a new device type is added

approvals.approved_version: network functions list signed for this period
the same signed network functions list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes repair notes stay free text, so the filing pass rarely completes a record. The high case assumes complete forms file themselves, while the choice of functions and every gap still take administrator time. Staff monitoring is not counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The administrator leaves routine mail filters and log extracts to signed jobs, and keeps the week for virus exceptions, access grants and user conversations.
reach: System users get a plain reply about their system problem instead of a raw console paste.
The network architect can read which network access was signed and which log extract is current.
skills_to_grow: Separate a virus rule that a filter can apply from mail a person must still read.
Keep a user conversation as a conversation, and file only the outcome they agreed.
State an access grant as a version with an owner and an end date.
role.ambitious_version: Mail filters, access grants and log extracts all run from a signed version, and the user conversation stays a person.
